content.text:
Suspense isn't crashing — the system is killing it. It's a memory kill by `systemd-oomd`, which kills the app's whole systemd unit.

**The evidence** (journal, Sep 27)
```
20:13:49 suspense@3c21d92…service: systemd-oomd killed 151 process(es) in this unit
20:13:49 Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
20:13:53 Failed with result 'oom-kill'
20:13:53 Consumed 2h 3min CPU, 18.9G memory peak, 17.2G memory swap peak
```
Other sessions show the same shape: 20 G peak at 16:36, 20.2 G at 19:33, 19.5 G at 00:26. Your machine has 30 G of RAM and 30 G of swap, so at those peaks the kernel is thrashing and `oomd` steps in.

**Why the unit gets that big**
Everything the agents start is a child of the app, so it all counts in the app's unit. Right now, 90 seconds after launch, the unit is at **7.2 GB**:

| Process | RSS |
|---|---|
| a `cargo test` binary (debug, GPUI UI tests) an agent is running | **1.95 GB** |
| `suspense` itself | 1.7 GB |
| 2 × `rustc` | ~0.4 GB each |
| 4 × `claude -p` | ~0.3 GB each |
| `target/release/octree-fps` (an app an agent launched) | 0.46 GB |
| `piton lsp`, plus two defunct `piton` children | small |

With two or three tasks running at once, each building and testing, that easily triples. The UI dying is collateral: `oomd` kills the unit, not the worst process.

**Fixes, most effective first**
1. **Get agent work out of the app's unit.** Start the harness with `systemd-run --user --scope -- claude …` (or `--slice`), so a runaway build is killed instead of your window. Alternatively set `ManagedOOMPreference=avoid` on the app unit and `omit` on the agents' slice.
2. **Cap the builds.** `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` and a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for agent runs. GPUI UI tests are the heaviest thing here: a single debug test binary is 2 GB, and running several at once is what pushes the peak to 19 GB. Telling agents in the Code/Chain prompts to run focused tests (`cargo test <name>`) rather than the whole suite would help a lot.
3. **Bring the app's own 1.7 GB down.** `.suspense/history` is now **295 MB across 258 records**, all loaded at startup and replayed into tasks with markdown state kept per row. The compact-record change we discussed would cut most of it; keeping only recent tasks' markdown in memory would cut the rest.
4. **Limit how many tasks run at once,** or at least warn: three concurrent Chain tasks means three agent builds.
5. **Reap the `piton` zombies** (two defunct children), small but easy.
6. **Restart on kill:** add `Restart=on-failure` to the unit so a kill doesn't lose the window, though it's better to prevent it.

Quick check next time it happens: `journalctl --user -u 'app-com.piton*' | grep -i oom` will confirm it's the same cause.
